# QS-CFW-1466-55 Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (52100)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Part: CFW-1466-55

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 produced in Plant P2 from material grade 52100. It applies to all production forgings, finishing, and final inspection prior to release to assembly or shipment. The intent is to ensure mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy necessary for bearing performance while minimizing false rejects through targeted inspection and documentation.

Requirements table
- The table below lists the critical characteristics and mandatory acceptance criteria for part CFW-1466-55.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Material grade | 52100 (as specified on the drawing and order) |
| Hardness | The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 36-41 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is ±0.05 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 32.2 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cracks, and other defects that compromise machining or function; acceptable machining mark patterns are defined on the drawing. |
| Finish operations | All finishing operations must maintain specified dimensional and metallurgical requirements prior to final inspection. |

Inspection method
- Overview: Final inspection is performed on the finished part after all machining and heat treat operations. Inspection is focused on the characteristics in the requirements table, with emphasis on hardness, bore size, and verification that forging weight did not exceed permitted handling/load limits.

- Hardness verification: Hardness shall be verified using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Perform measurements on machined surfaces representative of the bearing race. Record individual hardness readings and the location of each reading relative to the drawing. When multiple readings are taken on a single ring, report the range and note any local anomalies that indicate inhomogeneity or improper heat treat. Use the recorded data to confirm that the part meets The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 36-41 HRC. Calibration status of the hardness tester shall be current and traceable to the laboratory calibration system; calibration records must be retained with the inspection lot documentation.

- Dimensional verification: Bore diameter inspection shall be performed using calibrated bore gauges or equivalent measuring devices capable of resolving to the specification tolerance. Measurement locations must match the drawing characteristic positions. Measure and record bore size, and compare to The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is ±0.05 mm. If the measured bore is out of tolerance, tag the part as nonconforming and proceed to nonconformance handling. For assemblies that require runout or concentricity checks, perform those checks against the reference surfaces specified on the drawing and document results.

- Weight control: Weigh each forged blank after forging and prior to any material removal operations to ensure handling and tooling limits are respected. The forging process must not produce blanks in excess of The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 32.2 kg. If a blank exceeds this value, it must be segregated and reported as a process deviation; refer to nonconformance handling below.

- Surface and metallurgical checks: Visually inspect for surface discontinuities; use magnification as required for borderline cases. If indications suggest subsurface defects, use accepted non-destructive methods available in P2 to confirm condition. Metallurgical review is required when hardness or visual anomalies are found; document microstructure checks in the inspection record when performed.

- Sampling and lot records: Inspect every finished part for the characteristics in the table. For operations where statistical sampling is used for process control, maintain records that link sampled results to the affected production runs and to the individual parts when deviations occur. Inspection records shall include heat number, hardness readings, bore measurements, forging weight, operator, and inspector signatures or electronic approval, and reference to the drawing revision used for machining.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation: Any part that does not meet the requirements listed in the requirements table is nonconforming. Mark nonconforming parts clearly and segregate them from conforming inventory in a controlled area to prevent unintended use.

- Documentation: For each nonconforming part, complete a nonconformance report that includes part number, serial or batch identifiers where applicable, description of the nonconformity, measured values and locations, responsible operator, and inspector. Attach supporting inspection records, hardness printouts, weight records, and photographs if helpful for root cause assessment.

- Disposition options: Allowed dispositions include rework to drawing tolerances when feasible, use-as-is with documented engineering concession, scrap, or return to forging process for correction. All dispositions require approval by quality and engineering authority designated in Plant P2. Rework proposals must describe the corrective action, the inspection steps to verify compliance, and any impacts on material properties. Concessions granted must include justification and any additional inspection or labeling required to ensure safe use.

- Examples and rationale:
  - Example: If a bore measures outside The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is ±0.05 mm but material hardness is within the specified range, evaluate whether material removal within drawing limits can restore compliance without compromising section properties. Document the proposed correction and obtain approvals before proceeding.
  - Example: If hardness reading is below The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-1466-55 (CFW-1466-55) is 36-41 HRC., perform a metallurgical assessment and review heat treatment records. Do not return parts to stock until root cause is determined and corrective actions are implemented.

- Records to keep: Retain inspection records, nonconformance reports, disposition approvals, and calibration certificates for tools used in these inspections in the document control system for Plant P2. Records must be sufficient to trace the condition and disposition of each nonconforming part and to support corrective action investigations.

Revision control and note
- This document is controlled as Rev B. Any change to acceptance criteria or inspection methods requires a revision and documented approval through the P2 quality system. Related documents: none.
